correctness.rationale: The graph-gradient map on a tree is onto, so the induced Lipschitz norm equals the largest absolute row sum of the exact edge-gradient semigroup. The scalar and 2x2 mode decomposition yields explicit coefficients. A positive Green convolution proves strict hub-row dominance; strict coefficient signs classify every positive-time extremizer. Differentiation and a controlled large-m time choice establish the transition and sharp supremum three. The actual included checker passed exact Taylor identities through degree eight and 81 separately computed tree-cut W1 comparisons; finite tests are corroboration, not the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: Balanced double stars are a canonical, infinitely parametrized two-branching-hub tree family. The nontrivial analytic obstruction is to prove which edge gradient controls the sharp global semigroup norm despite time-changing coefficients. Resolving this yields a complete all-time norm, rigidity of maximizing potentials, the first two-hub amplification threshold and sharp asymptotic saturation of the diameter-three transport ceiling. This is a structural heat-transport benchmark rather than an arbitrary finite invariant or a restatement of tree curvature.
